_comment: Storefront colour name -> the hex the theme paints its swatch with. Single source of truth for the shrine-theme-pro setting Theme settings > Color swatches > Predefined custom colors. Generate the paste block with `python scripts/swatches.py render`; verify the live store and live theme against it with `python scripts/swatches.py check`.
_mechanism:
snippets/product-variant-options.liquid splits settings.swatches_predefined_colors_list on '

', splits each line on '=', strips both halves, and compares the left half to the option value name with Liquid ==, which is exact and case sensitive. No match leaves custom_color empty, the swatch renders style='--bg-color: ' and the circle comes out white. That, not any product data, is why Navy Blue, Coffee and Dark Gray were blank while Black and Maroon worked: the setting had never been touched and still held the theme's factory default of twenty generic CSS colours, which contains Black and Maroon and not the rest.
_why_one_hex_per_name: The list is global and keyed on the name alone, so a colour name carries the same hex on every product on the store and nothing per-product can override it. Two garments may not hold the same name for different colours. That is what forced the 18 Sep 2026 rename: three different greys across the catalogue had only two names between them.
_provenance: Every hex is the median fabric colour of the REAL Tapstitch mockup for that colourway, white print excluded, from artifacts/photo-mockup-spike/true_colors_all.json and documented in docs/photo-mockup-plan.md. NOT sampled from the on-model photos: those are AI recolours of a lit base shot and read several points lighter, which would put every swatch off its own garment in the same direction. Where two garments share a name the value is the mean of their readings and _samples keeps both, so a future change is judged against the readings rather than re-derived; the widest disagreement is Black at under 10 units of RGB distance.

_retired._note: Names carried only by the 40 old DRAFT tees, a dead line that is never published. Listed so `swatches.py check` reports them as knowingly ignored rather than as missing swatches.
